technical_and_design_decisions: The new channel configuration library will be implemented in Go, aligning with Hyperledger Fabric's primary language ecosystem to ensure seamless compatibility with existing Fabric proto definitions, cryptographic libraries, and tooling.

All required data structures, proto definitions, and core logic will be copied and adapted from existing Fabric open-source code (genesisconfig, configtxgen, configtxlator, cryptogen, peer packages) rather than importing the full existing packages, to meet the specification requirement of not using existing Fabric packages directly and avoiding unnecessary dependency bloat.

The U1 read set tampering detection feature will be implemented as an optional, configurable flag in the Fabric peer's transaction validation logic, defaulting to disabled to preserve backward compatibility with existing Fabric networks.

All cryptographic operations (MSP handling, transaction signing) will leverage Fabric's existing official crypto libraries to ensure generated signatures and MSP structures are fully compatible with Fabric orderer and peer validation logic.

The library will have zero external network dependencies, as required by U2, with all required configuration and cryptographic material passed explicitly as function inputs rather than loaded from external sources or configuration files.

All generated configuration structures and transactions will be validated against outputs of existing Fabric tooling (configtxgen, configtxlator, cryptogen, peer signtx) to ensure semantic equivalence as required by all user story acceptance criteria.
assumptions: The development team has full read access to the Hyperledger Fabric public source code repository, including all proto definitions, existing tooling implementations, and official integration test assets (sample configtx.yaml, MSP folders, test channel configurations).
Existing Fabric integration test assets are available for use in validating the equivalence of generated structures and transactions to outputs of official Fabric tooling.
The read set tampering detection feature (U1) can be implemented via a peer configuration flag without requiring changes to core Fabric consensus or ordering logic.

The detached signature format used for channel configuration updates is fully compatible with existing Fabric orderer and peer signature validation logic, so no modifications to core Fabric validation code are required beyond the U1 read set check.

All required proto definitions for channel configuration, ConfigUpdate, ConfigGroup, and related structures are available in the Fabric proto repository and can be legally copied and adapted into the new library per Hyperledger Fabric's open-source license.

activities.activity_name: Project Setup and Existing Code Analysis
activities.activity_description: Set up development workspace, clone Hyperledger Fabric source repository, analyze existing implementations of configtxgen, configtxlator, cryptogen, peer signtx, and transaction validation logic to identify reusable/adaptable code for the new library and U1 feature.

activities.activity_name: U1 Read Set Tampering Detection Implementation
activities.activity_description: Implement optional peer-side transaction validation logic to compare read set values against local world state during endorsement, invalidating transactions with mismatched read sets to prevent propagation of tampered data, with a configurable flag to enable/disable the feature.

activities.activity_name: U2 Library Structure and Core Type Definition
activities.activity_description: Set up standalone Go module for the channel configuration library, copy and adapt required proto structures (Profile, ChannelConfig, Application, Orderer, etc.) from Fabric's genesisconfig package, and define the public API for the CreateChannelTx function as specified.

Implement the CreateChannelTx function to generate proto-encoded genesis blocks matching the output of configtxgen, using adapted logic from existing Fabric configtxgen code without importing the original genesisconfig or viper packages.

Write and execute tests to verify that genesis blocks generated by CreateChannelTx are proto.Equal to blocks generated by configtxgen using the integration test suite's configtx.yaml and MSP folders, per U2 acceptance criteria.

Implement public function to sign a ChannelUpdate transaction using explicitly provided key material (not derived from configuration), generating a detached signature compatible with Fabric's signature validation logic.
